summary: Iteration 2 backend: ALL 19 new role-gate/approval tests pass + 26 regression tests from iteration 1 still pass (45/45 = 100%). Verified: admin-only staff creation (MLA 403); PA-only assign (MLA 403); worker status updates only on own issues (MLA 403, other-worker's issue 403); request-reassign clears assignee, sets Under Review, adds 'Reassignment Requested' timeline entry; PA-created visits return status='Pending Approval' (citizens cannot see); admin-created visits auto-publish + create notification; MLA approves pending visits -> Published + notification; PA cannot approve (403); PA-created devworks approved=false (citizens cannot see); admin-created devworks approved=true; MLA approve flips to true; PA approve 403; admin-only delete; notifications now carry created_by_name + recipients_count (>=1 for scope=all); households/{id} returns 'benefits' array. Frontend smoke: staff login page renders, but automated sidebar/UI verification was blocked because the email input is not type='email' (no data-testid on staff-login form fields). Did NOT manually validate role-aware sidebar visibility, IssueDetail panels, Visits Submit/Approve buttons, DevWorks pills, or Notifications recipients card via Playwright.

ui_bugs.issue: Email input is not type='email' and lacks data-testid, blocking automated UI tests

action_items: Add data-testid to staff login inputs (e.g. 'staff-email-input', 'staff-password-input', 'staff-login-submit') and to sidebar nav items so frontend automation can exercise role-aware UI.
Two minor pytest warnings: tests test_visits_pa_pending and test_devworks_pa_unapproved use 'return' instead of 'assert' (cosmetic only, all assertions before return execute).

Frontend role-aware sidebar/IssueDetail/Visits/DevWorks/Notifications UI changes were not E2E-verified by this iteration — recommend main agent self-test by logging in as MLA, PA, Worker and confirming the documented role-specific UI elements appear/hide as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/visits/{id}/approve: re-runs _publish_visit_notification on every call even if status was already Published — could create duplicate notifications if approve hit twice (no idempotency guard).
server.py request_reassign: stores assigned_to=None — list_issues for worker role filters by assigned_to=user_id so the reassigned issue correctly disappears from worker's list. Good.
server.py create_dev: when role=='admin' it auto-approves but never calls notification publish — by design (devworks don't notify), acceptable.
/api/visits citizen filter uses status='Published'; consistent across approve/create paths. Good.
